anti_overlap: Does NOT cover hook firing frequency (fd-claude-code-hooks-economy)
Does NOT cover MCP tool catalog (fd-mcp-server-hygiene)
decision_lens: What is the cheapest model that meets the precision/recall floor for this decision, and is the LLM-cost we pay today greater than the ML deployment cost?
focus: Identifies LLM-orchestrated classification, routing, and ranking decisions that could be served by traditional ML, embeddings, or deterministic rules
name: fd-llm-routing-replaceability
persona: Apply the perspective of an ML engineer who has replaced LLM judgment with cheaper learned models — they care about input vector design, the precision/recall floor of the classifier, retraining cost, and whether the LLM-cost being paid today exceeds the ML-cost (latency + retraining + monitoring) over expected volume
review_areas: Agent triage in flux-engine: today an LLM scores agent relevance to a target. Could embedding similarity (target text vs agent persona) plus a small classifier reach 90% precision at 1/100th the cost?
Skill routing: when user types a request, an LLM decides which skill to fire. Could a classifier on the user input text route to skill or 'no skill' faster?
Bead deduplication: `bd search` before `bd create` is currently the LLM's discipline. Could embedding-based fuzzy dedup (cosine over title+body) automate the search step?
Memory recall: deciding which memory file is relevant for a question is currently implicit LLM work. Could embeddings pre-filter, with the LLM only reading top-k?

Voice fidelity scoring: interfluence compare uses LLM judgment. Could an embedding-similarity + style classifier (sentence length, em-dash density, contrastive reframe count) score voice match deterministically?
Hook activation: hooks fire unconditionally today. Should some be gated by a deterministic predicate (regex match on user prompt + recent tool history) before paying LLM-orchestration cost?

severity_examples.condition: Per-run LLM cost is the dominant share of triage; replacement saves 5-15kt per /flux-drive invocation
severity_examples.scenario: An LLM-driven triage step is invoked on every flux-drive run but the agent-selection accuracy of an embedding-based router is within 2% — the LLM cost is unjustified

severity_examples.condition: Embedding-based dedup gate at bd create would prevent duplicates without LLM intervention
severity_examples.scenario: Bead deduplication relies on the user remembering to bd search first; bypassed in practice, leading to duplicate beads

severity_examples.condition: A regex+embedding classifier at the harness level could short-circuit before the LLM sees the prompt
severity_examples.scenario: Skill routing burns 200-500 LLM tokens per turn just to decide 'no skill needed'

source_domain: Traditional ML, embeddings + cosine, learning-to-rank, decision distillation
success_hints: For each candidate: name input vector, output, precision floor, approximate LLM-cost-displaced
Note training data source (cass logs, intercept distillation pattern)
Estimate complexity: XS=regex, S=embedding+cosine, M=xgboost, L=new infra
Identify the 5 highest-leverage replacements ranked by token savings
task_context: The Intercept project replaces LLM decision-gate calls with Haiku → log → distill xgboost. Find the next 5 candidates across Sylveste. Examples to triage: agent triage in flux-engine, skill routing on user input, bead deduplication on bd create, memory recall relevance, doc routing for /interpath:propagate, PR theme classification in /pr-triage, sprint phase classification, voice fidelity scoring in interfluence. For each, identify input vector, output, expected precision floor, and approximate LLM-cost-displaced.
